source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:17 (with Rashi; Bereshit Rabbah 34)
claim_en: הוצא — the WRITTEN form (ktiv) of the exit-command for the animals: SNAPSHOT stores the written skeleton as its own bare token — the instrument encodes the written/read (ktiv/qere) pair natively, two tokens side by side.

היצא — the READ form (qere) beside it, pointed: Bereshit Rabbah's teaching rides the difference ("COMPEL them to come out — for all the ark-months mating was forbidden"; Rashi carries it). SNAPSHOT: the pointed read-token locked.
מכל בשר ("of all flesh") — the bet carries a dagesh (doubling dot). SNAPSHOT agrees.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 7:2 (Ramah) — banked at gen_17
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION (banked from the gen_17 audit): הטהורה ("the pure one") at the ALTAR verse — mid-verse, outside the Ramah's rule that only the two verse-initial tokens (7:2, 7:8) are plene. SNAPSHOT writes it PLENE — a third full spelling the rule excludes; the letter locked, the deviation recorded.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:20 (Hilleli dispute; Ramah)
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION — ומכל העוף הטהור ("and of every pure bird"): the Hilleli codex records a dispute on this very word; the Ramah rules PLENE ("and every Torah token of this phrasing plene, except five defective ones listed elsewhere"). SNAPSHOT writes it DEFECTIVE (הטהר) — against the Ramah's ruling: the mirror-image of G20-04 in the same verse — plene where he rules defective, defective where he rules plene. Both letters locked.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:20 (Hilleli; Ramah; Zohar named)
claim_en: עלת ("burnt-offerings") — doubly defective (no vav in either slot), as the Hilleli copy and the Ramah rule: "and all Torah offering-language likewise doubly defective, except one." SNAPSHOT: the three-letter token locked at the first altar.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:20 (Ramah's exception rule)
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION — the Ramah's exception: exactly ONE offering-word in the Torah plene in its first slot — "build the altar of whole stones... and offer עולת" (Deut 27:6). SNAPSHOT holds TWO first-slot plene tokens: Deut 27:6 AND Num 28:24 (the daily offering of the festival week) — one more than the Ramah's count; the census locked, the surplus recorded.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:21 (all books vs Hilleli)
claim_en: וירח ("and He smelled") — "in all the books the yod with QAMATZ" (long a-vowel); the Hilleli margin records all-patach. SNAPSHOT: qamatz — the majority reading.

וירח — the Masorah pair, both in the Torah: God smells the pleasing scent (8:21) and Isaac SMELLS THE GARMENTS (27:27) — the Kitzur: read not בגדיו ("his garments") but בוגדיו ("his rebels"): "even the rebels of Israel will one day give fragrance." SNAPSHOT: exactly two tokens.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:21 (Bereshit Rabbah 34, R. Yudan); Kitzur (Masorah trio)
claim_en: מנעריו ("from his youth") — written DEFECTIVE, and R. Yudan's teaching rides the missing letter: "from the hour he STIRS (נעור) to leave his mother's womb." The Kitzur's trio spans out: "a man of war from his youth" (I Sam 17:33), "Moab settled from his youth" (Jer 48:11) — the fight with the inclination begins at birth; win it and rest like Moab on the lees. SNAPSHOT: the defective spelling locked; the trio's other legs are inheritance edges.

וקציר ("and harvest") — the Masorah pair, both in the Torah: the covenant of seasons (8:22) and Joseph's famine-forecast "neither plowing NOR HARVEST" (45:6): the promised rhythm and its recorded suspension. SNAPSHOT: exactly two tokens.
